chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:

Greed takes a person to the watering place but gets him back without letting him drink. It undertakes responsibility but does not fulfil it. Often the drinker gets choked before the quenching of his thirst. The greater the worth of a thing yearned for the greater is the grief for its loss. Desires blind the eyes of understanding. The destined share will reach him who does not approach it.

key_terms.مُورِدٌ: One that leads to a watering place/resource

ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual and practical consequences of greed according to Imam Ali in Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: In this saying from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (peace be upon him) employs the metaphor of the 'thirsty drinker' to illustrate how greed (al-ṭamaʿ) often causes spiritual or material harm before the desired goal is even attained. This reflects the Shia scholarly understanding of *al-ḥusn al-zann* versus *al-suʾ al-zann* in worldly pursuits, where excessive attachment blinds the heart (*aʿyun al-baṣāʾir*) to divine reality. The commentary highlights the paradox that while humans strive for what they value most, true success (al-ḥazz) may come to those who are not fixated on it, emphasizing reliance on God's decree.
